result:
I found the defect behind #276 and priced the fix offline, but the arm isn't registered: three of the four files the fix needs belong to other lanes. PR #323 is ready (analysis plus the named hunk, which the brief counts as complete) and preflight passes.

**The cause.** The issue's guess (`vk/draw.c:2294`, depthClampEnable) is wrong. The real cause is in `pgraph.c`, in `DEF_METHOD(NV097, SET_ZMIN_MAX_CONTROL)`: it stores only the ZCLAMP_EN bit and drops **CULL_NEAR_FAR_EN** (bit 0).

In the goldens, when that bit is set, silicon throws away a whole primitive if all its vertices have screen-space z below CLIP_MIN, or all above CLIP_MAX. It does this whatever ZCLAMP_EN says, and it tests z even on a w-buffered surface.
- **Evidence:** in all 12 failing captures, every Z=Inc block loses exactly quads 0–1 and 28–39. Quad 2 (z 7.3–10.06) and quad 27 (z 98.8–101.5) are kept, and the pattern is the same whatever w is.
- **Why only 12 fail:** the z-buffered NEARFAR_ZCULL captures already pass because our per-pixel clip hides every pixel of those primitives. On a w-buffer that clip tests w instead of z, so the WBuf_NEARFAR_ZCULL four don't pass.
- **IgnW:** the CULL_IGNORE_W bit has no visible effect on any golden.

**Priced offline** (`zmm_price.py`: our culled quads painted as background, then rescored against the goldens):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 12 target captures | 213,093 px differing (143,673 more than one step off) | 69,420 px, all one-step |
| other 20 ZMinMaxControl captures | unchanged | unchanged |

These are exactly the issue's own figures. The one-step residue matches the non-NEARFAR siblings (depth precision, not #276).

One leg is still a prediction: in the four CtrlFixed NEARFAR_ZCLAMP captures, a thin sliver of a rejected quad (it has a w=0 vertex) remains after painting. By my reading of `vsh-ff.c` that vertex's z comes out as 0, below the near clip, so the real rule should remove the sliver too. The device arm will confirm it.

**The fix** is in `docs/lanes/zclamp276/nearfar_cull.diff`, which applies cleanly to master:
- **`nv2a_regs.h`** (free): two defines.
- **`pgraph.c`** (held by lane.vshsubneg255): store bit 0.
- **`glsl/psh.h`** (held by lane.texvol283): one new state field.
- **`glsl/psh.c`** (held by lane.wbufdepth24, then texvol283, then wbuf31sel): discard the fragment when all three vertices' z are outside the clip range.

The new check is only generated when NEARFAR is set and the existing per-pixel clip doesn't already cover it. Every test gets NEARFAR on a z-buffer by default, and the suites that w-buffer or clamp (Depth clamp, W buffering, W param) write the control without NEARFAR. So across the test corpus it appears in exactly the 12 target captures, and every other shader is unchanged. That is the must-not-move argument.

The board request is `dispatch/board-requests/zclamp276.md`. `NOTES.md` has the arm spec for whichever lane applies the diff once the files are granted. I posted a `[lane.zclamp276]` comment on the issue and a `waiting:` comment on the PR.
